JJHC Varsity Practice — February 15, 2027

FieldValue
DateFebruary 15, 2027
Ice8:30 PM–9:30 PM ET (60 min)
RinkMcCann Ice Arena, Poughkeepsie NY
Shared withJunior Varsity
Focus themeBreakouts & D-zone exits
Roster~15 skaters + G Liam
Equipmentpucks, cones, tires/pads, whistle

ADM split target: ~50% skills / 30% hockey sense (SAG) / 20% systems.

Board cue: Concepts over choreography. What are we forcing the opponent to do?

Goalie (Liam): Read the system look (breakout rim, PP seam, PK shot lane). Talk early.

Clock

MinBlockADM
0–8A. Warm-up + puck flowSkills
8–28B. Stations (3× ~6–7 min)Skills / Contact
28–42C. Small-area gameHockey sense
42–54D. Systems / teamSystems
54–60E. Compete finisher + cool-downCompete

A. Warm-up (0–8)

Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players

  • Directions: Warm-up flow that links retrievals to first-pass exits. Skaters retrieve, hit a support target, and transition up ice without standing still. Great for D breakout habits.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WIgVxM39sZE

Flow: 0–2 easy laps with puck; 2–5 four-lane edges/C-cuts; 5–8 finish into the warm-up drill above with Liam seeing early shots.

B. Stations (8–28) — 3 groups, rotate ~6–7 min

Station 1 — sag|skills

Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game

  • Directions: 3v3 version of Gates of Buffalo. Teams score by completing passes through cone/tire gates while moving to open ice. Progress by shrinking gates or adding a defender.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=adueXqyfyNs

Station 2 — sag|systems

Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game

  • Directions: Cross-ice 3v2 that rewards quick east-west play and late support. Defense manages middle ice and sticks in lanes; offense looks for the third attacker.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MhoajOVDeGU

Station 3 — contact|skills

Puck Race to Possession Game

  • Directions: Objective New York Sirens forward Elle Hartje teaches players that winning a puck race isn't about being first to the puck—it's about winning the puck line. This competitive puck battle game develops body positioning on puck races, puck protection under pressure, and the ability to quickly transition into offense or defense on the second whistle. Setup Coach places a puck inside one of the faceoff circles.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1210465912

Contact sprinkle (inside Station 1 or 2 if time)

ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U)

  • Directions: 3v3 cross-ice with a center-line marker. After a D-zone retrieval, the team must skate behind its net before attacking. On a turnover in the attack zone, at least one F1 must pressure the puck. Reward immediate attack off a steal.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fDxI2eeEciY

C. Small-area game (28–42)

Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!

  • Directions: Open practice with a 12-player SAG so everyone is active immediately. Use a half-zone or below-dots box, short shifts, and a simple scoring rule. Sets tempo and compete early.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1vtqsH0Zw8I

Rules: continuous 30–45s shifts; sticks on ice; coach sets one constraint matching tonight’s theme.

D. Systems / team (42–54)

2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg

Keep 5v0 walkthrough under 2 minutes, then live. Concepts > choreography.

E. Finisher + cool-down (54–60)

Picket Fences Game (2 vs. 2 or 3 vs. 3)

  • Directions: Picket Fences is a great small area hockey game that can be setup as a 2 vs. The offensive team gets 2 points for scoring a goal and the defensive team gets 1 point by skating the puck between the tires . Setup: Teams are set up in one of the offensive zones in line with Dots.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/434166992

Last 2 min: easy skate / stretch; repeat board cue once.

One-goalie option (only 1 netminder tonight)

Optional: use only if Liam is the lone netminder. Everything above stays the plan of record; these swaps keep the same clock and tonight's focus (Breakouts & D-zone exits). Extra gear: 4–6 tires/pads + cones. Far-end net: pull it off its pegs (or turn it to the boards) and use the far end for the goalie-free game/targets. If a second goalie shows up, ignore this section.

A. Warm-up (0–8): Run *Defensive Transition Passing Warm-Up Drill for Hockey Players* as written — it doesn't need a goalie. Liam: 0–6 his own movement warm-up (stance, shuffles, T-pushes, butterfly slides) in his crease; 6–8 first shots — soft-to-firm from the hash marks, one at a time, no slappers.

B. Stations (8–28):

  • Station 1: *Gates of Buffalo 3 vs. 3 Game* — already goalie-free; run as written.
  • Station 2 (*Offense 3 v 2 Cross-ice Hockey Game*) → no-goalie: Neutral Zone Passing Station #1. Partners skate a cone lane making one pass per gap, drop-pass switch at the end, pass back; switch sides every rep. Keeps tonight's focus (Breakouts & D-zone exits) while Liam is at the net station. ▶ video
  • Liam's station — Station 3: *Puck Race to Possession Game*. Race in the circle; on the second whistle the winner attacks Liam and the loser defends — the defender scores by carrying it out through a blue-line gate. All three groups rotate through him, so keep reps short and controlled.
  • *Contact sprinkle (ADM F1 Forecheck Game (10U–18U))*: finish by carrying through a tire gate instead of shooting unless the group is at Liam's net.
  • Rest window: first 90 s of rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) — skaters at Liam's station finish on a tire in the net / upside-down net while he takes water and resets.

C. Small-area game (28–42), one net: 3 vs 3 Split Zone Game. Half a zone, 3 F vs 3 D on Liam's net; goal = 2 pts, D complete a pass and exit = 1 pt. Tonight's constraint: defenders need two passes before exiting; forwards forecheck 2-1. ▶ video

  • Prefer to keep *Start Practice with 12 Player Small Area Game!*? Play it to tire targets (two tires per end) instead of nets — no goalie needed.
  • Full sheet available? Split the 15: one group on Liam's net, the other at the far end in a goalie-free The Gate Game (no goalie); swap at 35:00 (the swap is Liam's 60–90 s breather). Half sheet only: 30–40 s shifts into the one-net game.

D. Systems (42–54), one net: *2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp* → One net: after a turnover the new offense must pass to the coach at the top of the circle before attacking Liam. Keep the 5v0 walkthrough on an empty net so Liam's first live rep is the first real one.

  • Alternate if it bogs down: Goal Line Small Area Game (USA Hockey). 2v2 on one net with Liam as neutral goalie; after every change of possession the puck must go below the goal line before attacking. Theme rule: the below-goal-line rule = breakout start; first pass up the strong side wall. ▶ video

E. Finisher (54–60): *Picket Fences Game (2 vs. 2 or 3 vs. 3)* → Already a one-net game (offense shoots on Liam; defense scores by skating the puck between the tires) — run it exactly as written. Last 2 min easy skate/stretch for everyone, Liam included.

Goalie workload (Liam):

  • Built-in breaks: 0–5/6 self-paced warm-up · 90 s in rotation 3 (≈22:00–23:30) · the 35:00 SAG swap · the 42–44 walkthrough on an empty net · 58–60 cool-down. Expect roughly 40–45 of 60 minutes in the net, so every block above is capped rather than continuous.
  • Shot quality: Count Liam's rim stops and puck-sets as reps; shots only at the end of an entry, never rapid-fire.
  • Tap-out rule: if his set time or rebound control slips (two soft goals in a row, late on lateral pushes), he hops out for 3–4 reps and skaters finish on the tire target, per USA Hockey's "let the goalie hop out for a few reps" guidance.
  • Coach reference: Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending). FutureProGoaltending: no rapid fire — leave a gap so he tracks every rebound; more zone looks, fewer slappers.

ADM self-check

  • Live decisions in almost every drill
  • Body contact / angling present (even if not the theme)
  • Liam got quality game-like looks
  • Transitions < 60 seconds

drill_library.title: John Jay Varsity — Drill Library
drill_library.html:
John Jay Varsity — Drill Library

Built for Coachy 60-minute ADM practice plans. Each entry has a short written setup and a public video URL (YouTube or Vimeo).

Where the drills webpage lives

  • Hub John Jay drill strip (6 IceHockeySystems Shorts): https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay
  • Private twin: https://franks-hub-private.pages.dev/#/johnjay
  • Config: `frank-hub/feeds.json` → `johnjay.videos` → IceHockeySystems
  • jjpuck.com Resources: menu exists but has no drill pages (empty). Club site is schedules/roster only.
  • Expanded sources: icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills, ADM Drill of the Month, USA Hockey articles.

Inventory: 38 drills with video links, plus 30 `one-goalie` additions (#39–68, added 2026-10-06). Machine-readable full scrape: `jj_drill_library.json` (54 entries).

Tags: `warm-up` | `skills` | `contact` | `sag` | `systems` | `goalie` | `one-goalie`

1. 1v1 Race to the Puck → 3v3 Transition Drill

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Start with a 1v1 race to a dumped puck, then layer into 3v3 transition as support arrives. Teaches win-the-puck-line body position, then immediate support and transition. Keep the whistle cadence high.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/lZgVOd8_TSI
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

2. 2 v 2 Angle Half-Ice Hockey Game with Defensive Reward

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Half-ice 2v2 with angling focus and a defensive reward rule (e.g., clear/score after a takeaway). Offense must move to support; defense angles first, then stick, then body. Continuous short shifts so everyone gets reps.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

3. 1 v 1 Angle & Gap Full Ice Hockey Drill

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: Full-ice 1v1 emphasizing angle and gap. Defender closes on an angle (stick on ice, outside shoulder lined up) while the attacker reads pressure and attacks open ice. Keep shifts short; reward the defender for forcing outside and the attacker for protecting the puck through contact.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WvmJ8qkkOn8
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

4. 3 v 3 Play Fast Game that Involves the WHOLE TEAM

  • Tags: `sag|skills`
  • Directions: Full-team 3v3 play-fast small-area game. Keep all lines rotating with short shifts so nobody stands. Emphasize first touch, immediate support, and transition the instant possession changes.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/8loIyjdiosg
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

5. 2 v 2 Transition Hockey Game from NHL Development Camp

  • Tags: `sag|systems`
  • Directions: 2v2 transition game used in NHL development camp. Offense attacks; on turnover, both sides transition immediately. Cue quick feet, first pass under pressure, and D activating or recovering without watching.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/041oIbGpvvg
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

6. What it means to be a good leader with Gold Medalist Hayley Scamurra

  • Tags: `systems`
  • Directions: Team talk / leadership clip. Use as a 60–90 second board or locker-room cue on compete, accountability, and how leaders set the tone for practice and games. Not an on-ice drill—pair with a compete block the same night.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/wwOIUxHVMTw
  • Source page: https://bottz77.github.io/franks-hub/#/johnjay

7. New Jersey 1v1 / 2v2 Contact SAG

  • Tags: `contact|sag`
  • Directions: Below-hash or half-zone boxes. Dump a puck; 1v1 then 2v2 with legal contact taught that night. Winner exits to a shot. Stop illegal hits immediately. Angle first, stick second, body third.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/shorts/PfpCL35u1tY
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/trainingmaterials

8. 1 v 1 Use The Net

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: 1 v 1 Use the Net from Jason Lammers is a great drill for all age levels that encourages offensive awareness and puck protection while the defenders work on angling and proper stick detail. The offensive team is trying to skate the puck through the gate while the defender is looking to strip the puck and score on net. Setup Setup a net and a gate as the goals.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1154377465
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/1-v-1-use-net

9. Angle Behind Net + Stick Check

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: O carries behind the net; X angles to force outside/into the corner and finishes with stick lift/press or controlled rub—no open-ice charge. Switch roles every few reps. Cue: stay slightly behind until the carrier clears the net, then close.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m88qmzCcERw
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=m88qmzCcERw

10. Puck Race to Possession Game

  • Tags: `contact|skills`
  • Directions: Objective New York Sirens forward Elle Hartje teaches players that winning a puck race isn't about being first to the puck—it's about winning the puck line. This competitive puck battle game develops body positioning on puck races, puck protection under pressure, and the ability to quickly transition into offense or defense on the second whistle. Setup Coach places a puck inside one of the faceoff circles.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/1210465912
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/puck-race-possession-game

11. Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush

  • Tags: `contact|systems`
  • Directions: The Pioneer 2 V 2 Rush from TJ Manastersky , the Head Coach of Brock University , practices attacking and defending the rush. It starts as a 1 V 1, and finishes as a 2 V 2. Setup On the 1st whistle, blue passes to red.
  • Video: https://vimeo.com/784999967
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/pioneer-2-v-2-rush

12. Partner Bump / Controlled Contact Confidence

  • Tags: `skills|warm-up|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Three side-by-side passing lanes in the neutral zone (or two longer lanes for fewer players) so six players go at once. Partners make one pass between each set of cones; at the last cone they turn toward each other, switch sides with a drop pass to the partner's forehand, and pass between each cone on the way back. Switch sides every rep for forehand and backhand reps.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LjDYuPzM6aY
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/neutral-zone-passing-station-1

61. Transition Pivot Races

  • Tags: `skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Two teams line up on either side of the center circle; coach at center with pucks. On the whistle skate forward until both feet are inside the blue line, pivot backward to a cone, pivot forward around it and back into the zone, then pivot backward to the second cone at center, open up to forward and race to the puck the coach places near the blue line. Open the hips without crossing over; the race adds urgency to footwork.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nsBIiBy02Mw
  • Source page: https://www.icehockeysystems.com/hockey-drills/transition-pivot-hockey-races

62. Circle 2v1 / Keep-Away Series (1 or 0 goalies)

  • Tags: `skills|sag|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Version 1: two attackers stay behind a drawn line and pass through a faceoff circle (one defender inside with an active stick) for one-timers. Version 2: 2v1, 2v2 or 3v1 inside the circle using the circle edge or bumpers as the boundary. Version 3: monkey-in-the-middle with passers on the rim moving the puck quickly around 1–2 defenders inside (4v2). Versions 2–3 run with no goalie at all.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RyLQIUL6Pek
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RyLQIUL6Pek

63. Tire Deke & Shoot Station

  • Tags: `skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Players skate with a puck, deke around a tire, and take a quick shot on goal in a continuous, high-rep station. On one-goalie nights shoot into a shooter tutor, an upside-down net, or tires/targets in an empty net so the goalie is free for another station. Cue head up on the approach and release in stride after the deke.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K5fqjKMuk5k
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K5fqjKMuk5k

64. Upside-Down Net Target Shooting (no goalie)

  • Tags: `skills|one-goalie`
  • Directions: When there is no goalie for a station, lay a spare net on its back and push it against the standing net so only a narrow strip near the crossbar stays open. Players shoot and finish at the small target, which rewards elevating the puck under control and keeps shooting stations alive without a netminder. Pucks only — nobody stands in the crease.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln-puBCmBvg (note: Needs a spare net from the rink.)
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ln-puBCmBvg

65. Shooting Recovery Drill (2 shooters, goalie reset)

  • Tags: `goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Goalie-specific drill from the OHL Coaches Conference clip: two shooters alternate — a low shot, the goalie recovers to his feet and sets on the next shooter — then progress to setting up on the rebound before moving to the next shooter. Short, controlled reps that build recovery and tracking habits. Ideal for the goalie's first 2–3 minutes of shots while skaters run a no-goalie station.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=64Aw6F2d9Ak
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=64Aw6F2d9Ak

66. Goalie Workload: Engage Goalies at Practice (USA Hockey)

  • Tags: `goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: USA Hockey coaching tip: give goalies a real warm-up at the start (goalie coach or an assistant) and choose team drills that train game situations, such as stopping/setting pucks behind the net in 2-on-1s. Pair it with USA Hockey's goaltending guidance: quality of reps over quantity, let the goalie reset and track the rebound between shots, and in high-volume drills let them hop out for a few reps — skaters shooting at an empty net for a few reps doesn't ruin the drill.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=g-GT6LRA9Nw
  • Source page: https://www.usahockey.com/news_article/show/1352978

67. Goalie Workload: Preparing Goalies for Practice (Jeff Lerg)

  • Tags: `goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: The Coaches Site talk by Jeff Lerg: in a poll of 153 goalies most wanted a warm-up with a coach first and preferred small-area games later, after they had seen pucks. Goalie reps should include pre-shot movement, lateral plays and traffic like real games; when ice is limited, a coach can work the goalie in a corner while the team runs a no-goalie or one-goalie game. Goalies own their movement warm-up while skaters warm up.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ocit0BtG3Sw
  • Source page: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ocit0BtG3Sw

68. Goalie Workload: Goalie-Friendly Practice (FutureProGoaltending)

  • Tags: `goalie|one-goalie`
  • Directions: Advice for head coaches on not wearing goalies out in practice: drop rapid-fire drills, build a gap between shots so the goalie can track the rebound into the corner, and train in proportion to games (more zone-play looks, fewer endless line rushes and slappers from the top of the circles). Make warm-ups for the goalie, not the shooters, and occasionally track practice save percentage so every puck matters.
  • Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ywcijl1ak_c
